title: Low-weight Pauli dynamics and truncation error

circuits of disjoint-support Hermitian Pauli rotations, with explicit
locality, angle, step-count, and cutoff hypotheses. Develops a faithful
matrix representation, Pauli coefficient reconstruction, finite Schur
bounds, and reusable scalar multi-jump ladder estimates. Also proves a
repeated product-formula layers must count toward the layer exponent.
This is the norm-level analysis, not a formalization of expectation-value
accuracy, Hamiltonian approximation, or the paper's full algorithm.

summary: Formalizes the Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic function fields of one variable
through the adelic route. Divisors are indexed by intrinsic places (discrete rank-one
valuation subrings containing the constants), with an equivalence to a two-chart
coordinate model via Ostrowski's theorem. The development builds Riemann–Roch spaces,
the genus, an intrinsic adele space, Weil differentials and the canonical class, and
proves Riemann's inequality, the duality theorem, Riemann–Roch, Clifford's inequality,
and the standard corollaries. As an application it shows that a Weierstrass elliptic
curve has genus one and identifies its degree-one places with the class group of the
coordinate ring compatibly with the group law.

title: Bounds for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal constant
Proves that the weak type (1,1) constant c_2 of the centered maximal
operator over axis-parallel squares is at least the explicit radical
phi, approximately 1.68551, using a weighted periodic lattice and
integrable approximations. Also proves c_d <= 2^d in every natural
dimension and 1.685 < phi < 1.686. The operator acts on real-valued
integrable functions, with Lebesgue outer measure of strict level
sets. Includes the maximal-function API, a Vitali covering argument,
lattice witnesses, smearing estimates, and the limiting lower bound.
No optimality of phi is claimed.
